title: Geometry quiz
description: Ten questions drawn at random from a bank of fourteen, covering polygon angles, tessellations, parallel-line angles and coordinates on a line segment.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a nonagon (9 sides)?
What is the interior angle of a regular 20-sided polygon?
A regular polygon has interior angles of $150^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
What is the sum of the exterior angles of a heptagon?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of **any** polygon add to $360^\circ$.

questions.prompt: A pentagon has angles $130^\circ$, $140^\circ$, $125^\circ$, $107^\circ$ and $c$. Find $c$.
A regular octagon tessellates on its own.
questions.explanation: False. Its interior angle is $135^\circ$, and $360 \div 135$ is not a whole number.
Three hexagons meet at every point, and $3 \times 120 = 360^\circ$.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $a$. Click the angle **alternate** to it.
questions.explanation: $a$ is between the lines on the left at the bottom crossing, so its alternate angle is between the lines on the right at the top crossing.

questions.prompt: The shaded angle is $a$. Click the angle **corresponding** to it.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are in the same position at each crossing.

questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $78^\circ$. What is its co-interior angle?
A trapezium has two angles of $102^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ at the ends of one of its parallel sides. What is the angle co-interior to the $60^\circ$ angle?
C is $(8, -3)$ and D is $(-12, 21)$. Find the point $\frac{1}{4}$ of the way along CD from C.
F is $(60, 70)$ and E is $(40, 50)$. Find the point $\frac{1}{10}$ of the way along FE from F.
questions.explanation: From F to E: $-20$ and $-20$. A tenth is $-2$ each: $(58, 68)$.
